learning_outcomes.text: Explain and interpret theoretical experimental results, technical documentation, phenomena and processes in the field of mechanical engineering.
Present and define the manufacturing process, technological process and its elements.
Present the types of semi-finished products, their preparation method and correct selection in the manufacturing process of a part.
Address the manufacturability of the construction.
Design technological processes based on the principle of operation differentiation.
Method of processing different types of surfaces.
Knowledge of current trends in manufacturing technologies.
Create skills to design and use different technologies.
Select and apply evaluation criteria, principles and methods for identifying, modeling and experimenting mechanical phenomena and processes.
Develop professional projects of medium complexity by selecting, combining and using concepts, principles, methodologies and technologies in the field of mechanical engineering.
Select and analyze specific bibliographic sources in the field of mechanical engineering.
Demonstrate autonomy in learning specific mechanical engineering issues.

Respect ethical principles, norms and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient and responsible work strategy in making decisions to solve problems.
Integrate into the work group and apply relationship and efficient work techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously inform and document himself in his field of activity by adequately using efficient lifelong learning methods and techniques.
Develop professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Chapter 1. Industrial processes. Production process. Technological process: definition, types of technological processes. Methods, procedures, technological variants.

Chapter 2. Semi-finished products used in machine building. Economic calculation of these. Types of semi-finished products (laminates, castings, forgings, etc.) and their technological characterization. Criteria for selecting semi-finished products. Shape criterion and economic criterion. Preparation of semi-finished products for mechanical machining by chip removal.

Chapter 3. Manufacturability of construction. Analysis of the part definition drawing. Definition of the concept. Factors determining the manufacturability of the construction, machinability, establishment of setting bases and rational dimensioning, constructive shape, precision and surface roughness, unification and standardization of parts.

Chapter 4. Machining precision. Technical-economic analysis of machining precision. Notions of machining precision. Analysis of machining precision using statistical-mathematical methods. Categories of errors. Empirical distributions and their parameters. Normal distribution. Determination of machining precision using frequency diagrams and point diagrams. Statistical control methods. Factors influencing machining precision. Theoretical machining errors. Errors caused by semi-finished product installation. Errors caused by inaccuracies in the execution of technological system elements. Errors caused by wear of technological system elements. Errors caused by adjusting the technological system to the working dimension. Errors caused by heating the technological system elements. Force field of the technological system. Elastic deformations caused by cutting forces. Static instability of the cutting process. Dynamic instability, self-oscillations. Deformations caused by forces. Measures to limit the influence of factors on mechanical machining precision. Use of dimension chains in determining machining precision. Dimensions, dimension chains, closing elements and their precision. Methods for solving all dimension chains.

Chapter 5. Surface condition. General notions. Factors influencing surface condition, surface asperities and surface layer. Influence of physical-mechanical properties of materials. Influence of tool geometry. Influence of cutting regime parameters. Influence of cooling-lubrication fluids. Influence of surface roughness on the operational behavior of parts. Influence on wear resistance. Influence on fit character. Influence on corrosion resistance. Influence on fatigue resistance.

Chapter 6. Design of mechanical machining technological processes by chip removal. Calculation of the final cost of part machining. General notions. Initial data required for design. Procedures for developing technological processes. Process of operation differentiation. Process of operation concentration. Design of technological processes according to the principle of operation differentiation. Selection of semi-finished product. Verification of part manufacturability. Establishment of mechanical machining operation sequences: classical method, computer-aided method. Calculation of machining allowances and intermediate dimensions: classical and computer-aided. Optimization of cutting regimes: criteria, objective function, constraint function. Work standardization. Calculation of the final cost of part machining.

Chapter 7. Machining of external cylindrical surfaces. Classification of parts with external cylindrical surfaces. Turning of external cylindrical surfaces. Milling of external cylindrical surfaces. Grinding of external cylindrical surfaces. Smoothing of external cylindrical surfaces.

Chapter 8. Machining of internal cylindrical surfaces. Conditions imposed on machined surfaces. Hole machining by drilling. Hole enlarging. Hole counterboring. Conical counterboring. Reaming. Complex hole machining. Hole boring. Turning of internal cylindrical surfaces. Internal grinding. Hole broaching. Methods for smoothing cylindrical surfaces.

Chapter 9. Machining of plane surfaces. Machining of plane surfaces by planing and slotting. Machining of plane surfaces by milling. Turning of plane surfaces. Broaching of plane surfaces. Grinding of plane surfaces. Methods for smoothing plane surfaces.

Chapter 10. Machining of conical and profiled surfaces. Turning of conical surfaces. Grinding of external and internal conical surfaces. Machining of profiled surfaces by turning. Machining of profiled surfaces by milling. Grinding of profiled surfaces.

Chapter 11. Thread machining technology. Machining of threads with cutting tools and threading combs. Machining of multi-start threads. Machining of external threads with die. Machining of threads with threading heads. Swirl threading. Machining of internal threads with taps. Thread milling. Rolling of external threads. Thread grinding. Machining of conical threads.
Chapter 12. Machining of keyways and splines. Machining of keyways. Machining of external splines. Machining of internal splines.

Chapter 13. Gear cutting processes. Milling of cylindrical gears with hob cutters. Slotting of cylindrical gears with gear shaper cutters. Slotting of cylindrical gears with comb cutters. Grinding of cylindrical gears with biconical discs (Niels method). Grinding of cylindrical gears with dish-shaped discs (Maag method).
Work safety.
Machining errors caused by placing semi-finished products on prisms for mechanical machining.
Machining errors caused by placing semi-finished products between centers for mechanical machining.
Machining errors produced by setting the tool to the working dimension using the trial piece method.
Machining errors caused by clamping semi-finished products for mechanical chip removal machining.
Setting the technological system for swirl threading and determining the factors influencing thread precision.
Copy machining of cylindrical toothed rollers using a modular disc cutter.
Setting the technological system for machining the teeth of cylindrical gears with straight and helical teeth using a modular hob cutter and determining machining errors.
Design of manufacturing technologies for a given part on universal machine tools.
Analysis of the execution drawing, verification of manufacturability, selection of the semi-finished product.
Establishment of the technological route.
Calculation of machining allowances and intermediate dimensions.
Determination of machining regimes.
Technical standardization.
Evaluation of economic efficiency.
teaching_methods: Debates based on Power Point presentations
Short recap of previous course notions
Discovery learning models facilitated by direct/indirect exploration of reality (experiment, demonstration, modeling)

assessment_methods.method: Exam/Verification (includes systematic observation, individual/team assignments, case study report, formative and summative evaluation tests)
Laboratory activity (completion of laboratory sheets, laboratory colloquium)
Project (design activity, project finalization, project presentation)

assessment_rules: The result of the final evaluation for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of corresponding study credits. All laboratory works must be completed, allowing only one overdue laboratory work to be recovered.
